questions.q: A county hospital Nursing Officer in Charge observes persistently high staff turnover among KRCHN cadres and declining documentation quality. According to the National Nursing and Midwifery Policy 2022–2032 and NCK Code of Conduct for managers, which strategic action best addresses both retention and professional standards simultaneously?
options: Link mentorship and CPD programmes to appraisal systems and succession planning
Increase overtime allowances and issue structured verbal warnings for documentation gaps
Restrict leave allocations and reassign senior staff only to clinical duties
Outsource documentation audits to an external firm with quarterly reporting
questions.explanation: The Policy prioritises strengthening nursing leadership capacity, workforce management and CPD to reduce attrition and improve quality. The Code requires mentoring, enabling environments, professional appraisal systems and succession management.

questions.q: Under the Nurses and Midwives Act Cap 257, which function of the Nursing Council of Kenya most directly empowers a facility Nursing Manager to enforce professional standards of care and staffing within a health institution?
options: Prescribing uniforms, badges and insignia for registered practitioners
Conducting licensing examinations and student indexing processes
Having regard to standards of nursing care, qualified staff, facilities and environment
Approving training institutions and regulating their curricula
questions.explanation: Section 9(1)(i) explicitly gives NCK the mandate to monitor and take measures regarding standards of nursing care, qualified staff, facilities and environment.

questions.q: In applying the Kenya Quality Model for Health (KQMH) Dimension 1 (Leadership), a facility manager must demonstrate which of the following as the highest-priority governance action?
options: Publishing the hospital mission statement on notice boards
Holding monthly staff motivational and recognition meetings
Purchasing new equipment for all nursing work stations
Ensuring regulatory compliance and establishing legal governance structures
questions.explanation: KQMH Standards 1.1.1 and 1.1.2 require management to ensure regulatory compliance and put in place governance structures aligned with legislation.

questions.q: A newly qualified KRCHN is asked by a senior nurse to administer a medication outside the documented scope for that cadre without counter-checking. According to NCK Scope of Practice principles and the Code of Conduct, the most appropriate professional response is:
options: Administer the medication to avoid conflict and report later
Perform the task only under direct senior nurse supervision
Refuse, document the request and escalate citing scope limitations
Accept the task if the patient is currently clinically stable
questions.explanation: Scope of Practice documents emphasise that nurses practise within the limits of their education, licence and competence. The Code requires upholding standards.

questions.q: Which leadership approach is most consistent with effective change management during implementation of a new nursing documentation system required by recent NCK policy briefs?
options: Autocratic directive with immediate sanctions for non-compliance
Staff involvement in barrier identification plus training and support
Laissez-faire allowing each unit to adopt or reject the system
Transactional rewards given only to the earliest adopters
questions.explanation: National Policy and leadership development programmes emphasise change management skills, quality improvement methodology and creating enabling environments.

questions.q: A BScN-prepared Nursing Services Manager is developing a facility staffing plan. Which combination best reflects current Kenyan norms, Scheme of Service principles and NCK policy briefs on nurse-to-patient ratios?
options: Fixed national ratios applied uniformly across all service areas
Minimum staffing calculated solely from available bed capacity
Staffing levels set exclusively by the current budget allocation
Context-specific ratios based on acuity, skill mix and outcomes
questions.explanation: NCK policy briefs and the National Policy emphasise optimum nurse-to-patient ratios that vary by service area and evidence-based workforce planning.

questions.q: According to the NCK Code of Conduct for nurse/midwife managers, which responsibility is specifically emphasised toward the profession itself?
options: Ensuring licensed practitioners, research support and ethical values
Providing direct clinical care on every allocated shift
Negotiating annual salary and allowance increments
Limiting staff access to external training opportunities
questions.explanation: The Code explicitly lists duties to the profession: uphold standards, ensure only qualified/licensed practitioners practise, foster research, promote ethical values and professional associations.

questions.q: In the WHO health system building blocks framework as applied in Kenyan governance and leadership training materials, which block is most directly strengthened when a Nursing Manager improves duty rostering transparency, performance feedback and CPD access?
options: Health financing mechanisms and resource allocation
Medical products, vaccines and technology systems
Human resources for health with service delivery linkages
Health information systems and data management
questions.explanation: Transparent rostering, feedback and CPD address the human resources building block while supporting service delivery quality and governance.

questions.q: A facility experiences recurrent medication errors. The most appropriate leadership response consistent with KQMH management review and continual improvement standards is:
options: Identify and publicly reprimand the individual nurses involved
Suspend all medication privileges pending external audit
Increase frequency of random drug counts and checks only
Conduct systems-based root-cause analysis and monitor learning
questions.explanation: KQMH requires management to continually review operations and support staff engagement in continuous quality improvement. Systems thinking aligns with modern patient safety principles.

questions.q: Which statement correctly reflects the differentiated leadership expectation between a KRCHN and a BScN graduate under current NCK Scope of Practice and Scheme of Service?
options: Both cadres hold identical leadership authority at facility level
KRCHN focuses on unit-level supervision; BScN on broader managerial roles
Only BScN-prepared nurses may supervise any nursing staff
KRCHN has no formal leadership role beyond direct patient care
questions.explanation: Scope of Practice and Scheme of Service differentiate preparation levels. Diploma prepares for clinical and unit supervision; degree adds managerial, educational and higher administrative roles.

questions.q: When resolving inter-professional conflict over task allocation in a multidisciplinary team, the Nursing Manager’s approach most consistent with NCK ethical leadership and good governance principles is:
options: Unilaterally reassign tasks based on existing hierarchy
Escalate immediately to the County Director without local attempt
Facilitate dialogue based on scopes, safety and documented agreements
Ignore the conflict to maintain surface team harmony
questions.explanation: Code of Conduct and Policy emphasise collaboration, respect for professional boundaries, patient-centred care and positive workplace culture.

questions.q: A County Nursing Officer is tasked with cascading the National Nursing and Midwifery Policy 2022–2032. The highest-leverage leadership action is:
options: Translating policy into county plans, indicators and capacity activities
Distributing printed copies of the policy to all facilities
Holding a single high-profile launch ceremony for stakeholders
Focusing solely on uniform and insignia compliance measures
questions.explanation: The Policy is a framework requiring translation into actionable strategies at national and county levels.

questions.q: A Nursing Officer in Charge discovers that several newly indexed KRCHN interns are performing procedures beyond the documented entry-level scope without structured supervision. The most appropriate immediate managerial action is:
options: Allow the practices to continue if no adverse events occurred
Issue a verbal warning only and continue as before
Reassign the interns permanently to non-clinical duties
Stop out-of-scope work, assess competence and escalate formally
questions.explanation: Scope of Practice and the Code require that only competent, licensed practitioners perform procedures within defined limits.

questions.q: Under KQMH Leadership standards, which of the following best demonstrates “management review and continual improvement”?
options: Holding an annual staff party to boost overall morale
Purchasing new uniforms for all nursing staff members
Reviewing performance data, closing gaps and documenting progress
Restricting staff meetings to maximise clinical work time
questions.explanation: KQMH Standard 1.2 requires management to continually review operations and support continuous quality improvement.

questions.q: A facility is experiencing high rates of missed nursing care. The Nursing Manager applies a leadership theory that matches style to staff competence and commitment. Which theory is being applied, and what is the most appropriate first step?
options: Trait theory – identify innate leader characteristics among staff
Situational leadership – assess readiness and adapt style accordingly
Great Man theory – wait for a natural leader to emerge
Transactional leadership – introduce financial penalties for missed care
questions.explanation: Situational leadership (Hersey-Blanchard) is widely taught in Kenyan nursing leadership curricula.

questions.q: When delegating a complex wound dressing to a junior KRCHN, the delegating nurse must ensure which of the following to remain accountable under NCK standards?
options: The task is completed regardless of the junior’s competence
Competence, clear instructions, supervision and retained accountability
The junior accepts the task verbally without further discussion
Documentation of delegation is optional if the patient is stable
questions.explanation: Delegation principles require assessment of competence, clear communication, appropriate supervision and retained accountability.

questions.q: According to the NCK Code of Conduct for nurse/midwife managers, which of the following is a specific duty “to the public”?
options: Prioritising staff leave requests over patient care needs
Limiting family involvement in all care decision processes
Focusing exclusively on facility cost-containment measures
Respecting dignity, privacy, information and resource advocacy
questions.explanation: The Code explicitly outlines public-facing responsibilities: dignity, privacy, confidentiality, information provision, quality promotion and resource advocacy.

questions.q: A County Director of Nursing Services is preparing a briefing on nursing workforce challenges. Drawing on recent NCK policy briefs and the National Nursing and Midwifery Policy, which combination of issues should receive highest priority?
options: Uniform colour variations across different health facilities
Preference for private-sector employment among nurses
Staffing gaps, ratios by area, documentation and leadership capacity
Elimination of all diploma-level training programmes
questions.explanation: Recent NCK policy briefs address staffing status, nurse-to-patient ratios, documentation gaps and CPD uptake.

questions.q: Which of the following best reflects the relationship between leadership and management in the Kenyan nursing context as presented in standard leadership and management curricula?
options: Leadership and management are identical and interchangeable
Only leadership is needed; management skills are now obsolete
Management is for BScN only; leadership is for KRCHN only
Management handles resources and processes; leadership influences people
questions.explanation: Kenyan training materials treat leadership and management as distinct yet interdependent competencies.

questions.q: A senior nurse manager is pressured by facility administration to falsify staffing returns submitted to the county and NCK. The most appropriate professional response guided by the Code of Conduct and Cap 257 is:
options: Refuse, document pressure, uphold accuracy and escalate properly
Comply to protect the facility’s funding and reputation
Alter only the figures least likely to be audited later
Resign immediately without further action or documentation
questions.explanation: The Code requires managers to uphold professional ethical values and ensure accurate data. Cap 257 mandates regard to standards of qualified staff.

questions.q: In the context of health facility governance structures required by KQMH and relevant legislation, the Nursing Manager’s primary accountability is best described as:
options: Solely to the medical superintendent for all clinical and administrative decisions
Accountability only to the county nursing director
Dual accountability — operational within the facility hierarchy and professional to NCK
No formal accountability beyond personal clinical practice
questions.explanation: Nurse managers operate within facility governance while remaining professionally accountable to NCK regulatory standards.

questions.q: A facility introduces a new electronic nursing documentation system. Six months later, uptake remains low and documentation quality has not improved. The most effective leadership response consistent with change management and KQMH is:
options: Mandate 100% compliance with immediate sanctions for non-users
Abandon the system and return to paper records
Replace all resistant staff with new recruits
Assess barriers, co-design solutions with users and monitor iteratively
questions.explanation: Effective change management requires diagnosis of barriers, participatory problem-solving, support and continuous monitoring.

questions.q: A Nursing Manager notices that staff consistently bypass the official referral pathway for critically ill patients. The most appropriate first managerial action consistent with KQMH governance and patient safety standards is:
options: Issue a facility-wide memo threatening disciplinary action
Conduct a rapid systems review of barriers and redesign the pathway
Instruct nurses to stop all referrals until further notice
Report every individual nurse who bypasses the pathway to NCK
questions.explanation: KQMH emphasises systems thinking, continual improvement and governance structures that support safe care.

questions.q: According to the NCK Code of Conduct, a nurse manager’s duty “to the practice” most clearly includes:
options: Ensuring every nurse works overtime without compensation
Restricting all staff from joining professional associations
Promoting quality care, appraisal systems, CPD, mentoring and safe practice conditions
Focusing exclusively on reducing the facility’s wage bill
questions.explanation: The Code explicitly lists these responsibilities under the manager’s duty to the practice.

questions.q: Which statement correctly reflects the application of accountability when a BScN Nursing Officer delegates a task to a KRCHN?
options: Once delegated, the BScN officer has no further responsibility
The KRCHN becomes fully accountable and the BScN officer is absolved
Accountability is shared equally with no clear primary responsibility
The BScN officer retains ultimate accountability while the KRCHN performs within scope
questions.explanation: Professional standards maintain that the delegator retains accountability.

questions.q: A facility is preparing for an external quality assessment under KQMH. The Nursing Manager’s highest-priority leadership action is:
options: Coaching staff on how to give “correct” answers during interviews
Ensuring actual compliance with standards and closing identified gaps
Hiding non-compliant records from assessors
Focusing only on physical appearance of the wards
questions.explanation: Genuine compliance and continuous improvement are the intent of KQMH.

questions.q: In the context of the National Nursing and Midwifery Policy 2022–2032, which leadership capacity area is identified as critical for reducing attrition and improving service quality?
options: Advanced clinical procedure skills only
Exclusive focus on industrial action skills
Skills in leadership, change management, QI and positive workplace environments
Mastery of financial accounting software only
questions.explanation: The Policy recognises gaps in managerial confidence and skills as drivers of attrition and suboptimal care.

questions.q: A KRCHN unit in-charge is asked to prepare the monthly nursing returns for submission. The most professionally correct approach is:
options: Estimate figures to make the unit look fully staffed
Omit sections that show shortages
Delay submission until the next quarter
Submit accurate data on staffing, workload and gaps, and use it to advocate
questions.explanation: Accurate reporting is a professional and regulatory obligation.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the relationship between the Nursing Council of Kenya and a facility Nursing Manager regarding standards of care?
options: NCK has no interest in facility-level practice
Only the County Director of Nursing can interact with NCK
Managers may ignore NCK standards if the facility has its own policies
NCK has statutory authority over standards; the manager is the first-line implementer
questions.explanation: Section 9(1)(i) of Cap 257 gives NCK this explicit mandate.

questions.q: When introducing a new infection prevention protocol, the most effective leadership sequence consistent with change management principles is:
options: Announce the protocol and immediately discipline non-compliant staff
Assess readiness and barriers, involve staff, train, implement, monitor and adjust
Leave implementation entirely to individual nurses
Implement only on day shifts
questions.explanation: Structured change management produces more sustainable adoption than pure authority or laissez-faire approaches.

questions.q: A BScN-prepared manager is developing a unit-level quality improvement project. Which starting point is most consistent with KQMH and modern QI methodology?
options: Selecting a problem based on personal preference
Waiting for the county to prescribe the project
Using available data to identify a high-impact measurable problem then applying PDSA
Focusing only on problems that require no resources
questions.explanation: Data-driven problem selection and structured improvement cycles are core to KQMH continual improvement.

questions.q: According to the Scheme of Service and Scope of Practice differentiation, which leadership function is more characteristically expected of a BScN Nursing Officer than a KRCHN?
options: Direct patient care only
Broader involvement in policy interpretation, programme coordination and higher-level planning
No leadership responsibility
Exclusive responsibility for laundry and catering services
questions.explanation: Degree preparation equips nurses for expanded managerial, educational and strategic roles.

questions.q: A nurse manager observes bullying behaviour by a senior staff member toward juniors. The most appropriate response guided by the Code of Conduct is:
options: Ignore it because the senior is clinically competent
Transfer the juniors to another unit without investigation
Address the behaviour promptly, protect affected staff and apply fair process
Publicly shame the senior nurse
questions.explanation: Managers are required to promote positive working environments and uphold professional conduct.

questions.q: Which of the following is the strongest indicator that a Nursing Manager is practising ethical leadership under NCK standards?
options: Popularity among staff
Ability to avoid all conflict
Success in reducing the nursing wage bill
Consistent alignment of decisions with ethics, safety, equity and accountability
questions.explanation: Ethical leadership is demonstrated by principled decision-making that upholds the Code and patient interests.

questions.q: In applying the management function of “controlling,” a Nursing Manager should primarily:
options: Focus only on punishing errors
Set standards, measure performance, identify variances and take corrective action
Avoid any form of monitoring to maintain staff morale
Delegate all monitoring to external auditors only
questions.explanation: Controlling closes the loop between planning and results when linked to standards, measurement and improvement.

questions.q: A facility has chronic shortages of basic nursing supplies. The most professional managerial response is:
options: Instruct nurses to improvise indefinitely without documentation
Blame the procurement officer publicly
Accurately document stock-outs, escalate and participate in solutions while maintaining safe practice
Stop all procedures that require the missing supplies without communication
questions.explanation: Accurate documentation, escalation and advocacy are professional responsibilities.

questions.q: Which leadership style is generally most effective when leading a team of highly experienced, competent and committed nurses through a complex quality improvement initiative?
options: Highly directive (telling)
Coaching or supporting/participative styles that leverage their expertise
Laissez-faire with no guidance
Purely transactional rewards and punishments
questions.explanation: High-readiness staff benefit from participative and supportive approaches.

questions.q: Under Cap 257 and NCK functions, which of the following is a legitimate basis for NCK to take action regarding a health facility?
options: The facility’s profit margin
Standards of nursing care, qualified staff, facilities, conditions and environment
The political affiliation of the facility manager
The colour of the nurses’ uniforms only
questions.explanation: Section 9(1)(i) explicitly gives NCK this mandate.

questions.q: A Nursing Manager is asked to implement a new national guideline that conflicts with long-standing local practice. The most appropriate leadership approach is:
options: Ignore the national guideline
Force immediate 100% compliance without discussion
Analyse the guideline, engage staff, support transition and monitor outcomes
Allow each nurse to choose whether to follow it
questions.explanation: Effective translation of national guidelines requires analysis, engagement, supported implementation and evaluation.

questions.q: Which of the following best demonstrates a Nursing Manager fulfilling the duty “to the profession” under the NCK Code of Conduct?
options: Discouraging staff from joining professional associations
Ensuring only qualified and licensed nurses provide services, upholding standards and promoting ethical values
Prioritising facility loyalty over professional standards
Limiting staff access to NCK communications
questions.explanation: These actions are explicitly listed in the Code as duties to the profession.

questions.q: In the context of health systems strengthening, when a Nursing Manager improves duty roster transparency, fair workload distribution and access to CPD, which WHO building block is most directly strengthened?
options: Health financing in isolation
Human resources for health (with positive effects on service delivery and governance)
Medical products and technologies only
Leadership and governance alone without HRH impact
questions.explanation: These actions primarily address the HRH building block.

questions.q: A newly appointed KRCHN unit in-charge feels unprepared for the leadership demands of the role. The most constructive professional action is:
options: Avoid all decision-making
Seek structured mentorship, utilise leadership development opportunities and build competence progressively
Resign immediately
Rely solely on personal clinical experience without further development
questions.explanation: The National Policy and NCK emphasise continuous professional development and leadership capacity building.

questions.q: A Nursing Manager is informed that a senior nurse has been practising without a valid practising licence for three months. The most appropriate immediate action is:
options: Allow the nurse to continue because of clinical experience
Quietly advise the nurse to renew the licence without formal action
Immediately stop the nurse from practising, verify status with NCK and escalate
Transfer the nurse to a non-clinical role without further investigation
questions.explanation: Only licensed practitioners may provide nursing services. Managers must ensure only qualified and licensed nurses practise.

questions.q: Which of the following best illustrates effective application of the management function of “organising” in a nursing unit?
options: Writing a vision statement
Clarifying roles, responsibilities, reporting lines and resource allocation
Conducting end-of-month performance appraisals only
Motivating staff through speeches
questions.explanation: Organising translates plans into structured work by defining roles, authority relationships and resource deployment.

questions.q: A BScN Nursing Officer is leading a multidisciplinary quality improvement team. Conflict arises between nursing and medical staff over task allocation. The most constructive leadership response is:
options: Unilaterally decide in favour of the nursing position
Facilitate structured dialogue grounded in scopes of practice, safety and mutual respect
Withdraw nursing participation from the team
Escalate immediately to the County Director without local resolution attempt
questions.explanation: Effective inter-professional leadership uses scope-informed dialogue and shared patient-centred goals.

questions.q: According to recent NCK policy briefs and the National Nursing and Midwifery Policy, which factor is most strongly associated with improved retention of nurses?
options: Strict enforcement of uniform guidelines only
Supportive leadership, CPD opportunities, fair workload and positive workplace culture
Longer working hours with higher overtime pay exclusively
Restriction of professional association membership
questions.explanation: Policy documents identify supportive leadership, CPD access, manageable workload and positive culture as key retention drivers.

questions.q: When a Nursing Manager applies “directing” as a management function, the core activities include:
options: Only writing policies
Guiding, supervising, motivating, communicating expectations and leading staff
Counting stock at the end of the month
Designing the facility organogram alone
questions.explanation: Directing involves the human side of getting work done through people.

questions.q: A KRCHN in-charge discovers that documentation of nursing care is consistently incomplete across the unit. The most appropriate initial managerial response is:
options: Publicly reprimand all staff at the next meeting
Conduct a structured assessment of barriers, provide support and monitor improvement
Stop all clinical work until documentation is perfect
Ignore the issue because the facility is understaffed
questions.explanation: Documentation gaps are a recognised NCK priority. Systems-oriented assessment and supportive improvement are more effective.

questions.q: Which statement correctly reflects dual accountability of a facility Nursing Manager in Kenya?
options: Accountability only to the facility CEO
Operational accountability within the facility hierarchy and professional accountability to NCK
Accountability solely to the County Nursing Director
No formal accountability beyond personal clinical competence
questions.explanation: Nurse managers operate within institutional governance while remaining professionally regulated by NCK.

questions.q: In situational leadership, when staff demonstrate high competence but variable commitment to a new protocol, the most appropriate style is:
options: Highly directive (telling)
Supporting or participating — sharing decision-making and providing encouragement
Delegating with no further involvement
Coercive punishment
questions.explanation: High competence with variable commitment calls for supportive/participative behaviours.
